questions.question: Why does the Transformer use self-attention instead of recurrence?
questions.gold_supporting_passage: The Transformer follows this overall architecture using stacked self-attention and point-wise, fully connected layers for both the encoder and decoder.
questions.expected_facts: It uses stacked self-attention and point-wise layers, avoiding recurrence in the core architecture.

questions.question: What is the formula for scaled dot-product attention?
questions.gold_supporting_passage: We call our particular attention "Scaled Dot-Product Attention". The input consists of queries and keys of dimension dk, and values of dimension dv.

questions.question: How does multi-head attention differ from one attention head?
questions.gold_supporting_passage: Multi-head attention allows the model to jointly attend to information from different representation subspaces at different positions.
questions.expected_facts: It projects queries, keys, and values into multiple subspaces, applies attention in parallel, concatenates, and projects the results.

questions.question: Does the Transformer paper prove that its architecture is optimal for spoken full-duplex dialogue?
questions.expected_facts: The approved library does not establish this claim.

questions.question: What positional information does the original Transformer add?
questions.gold_supporting_passage: Since our model contains no recurrence and no convolution, in order for the model to make use of the order of the sequence, we must inject some information about the relative or absolute position of the tokens in the sequence.
questions.expected_facts: It adds positional encodings to input embeddings; sinusoidal encodings are described and learned encodings are also possible.

questions.question: What is Moshi's theoretical and practical latency reported in the paper?
questions.gold_supporting_passage: Our resulting model is the first real-time full-duplex spoken large language model, with a theoretical latency of 160ms, 200ms in practice.
questions.expected_facts: The paper reports 160 ms theoretical latency and 200 ms in practice.

questions.question: Why does Moshi use a multi-stream setup?
questions.gold_supporting_passage: It generates speech as tokens from the residual quantizer of a neural audio codec, while modeling separately its own speech and that of the user into parallel streams.
questions.expected_facts: It models the user's and system's speech separately in parallel streams and generates speech tokens through the codec hierarchy.

questions.question: What does Moshi mean by Inner Monologue?
questions.gold_supporting_passage: We introduce Inner Monologue, which consists in first predicting text tokens as a prefix to audio tokens.
questions.expected_facts: It predicts time-aligned text tokens before audio tokens, enabling an internal textual stream associated with speech generation.

questions.question: Can the Moshi paper tell me the exact p99 latency of my own laptop with an RTX 3050?
questions.expected_facts: The paper's reported latency is not a measurement of this laptop.

questions.question: Moshi kya streaming ASR aur TTS support karta hai?
questions.gold_supporting_passage: We evaluate Moshi as a streaming ASR and TTS system.
questions.expected_facts: Yes, the paper evaluates Moshi for streaming ASR and TTS.

questions.question: What problem does Dynamic Chunking identify with fixed-vocabulary tokenization?
questions.gold_supporting_passage: Pre-processing steps such as tokenization remain a barrier to true end-to-end foundation models.
questions.expected_facts: Fixed-vocabulary tokenization is a preprocessing barrier and can have drawbacks for character-level robustness and languages with weaker tokenization heuristics.

questions.question: What is an H-Net in the Dynamic Chunking paper?
questions.gold_supporting_passage: Incorporating this into an explicit hierarchical network (H-Net) allows replacing the tokenization–LM–detokenization pipeline with a single model learned fully end-to-end.
questions.expected_facts: It is an explicit hierarchical network using learned dynamic chunking to replace the tokenization-LM-detokenization pipeline.

questions.question: Does Dynamic Chunking use manually annotated chunk boundaries as supervision?
questions.gold_supporting_passage: H-Nets ... qualitatively learn meaningful data-dependent chunking strategies without any heuristics or explicit supervision.
questions.expected_facts: The paper says the learned chunking strategies do not use heuristics or explicit supervision.

questions.question: Dynamic Chunking ke mutabik Chinese jaisi languages mein kya advantage ho sakta hai?
questions.gold_supporting_passage: The H-Net’s improvement over tokenized pipelines is further increased in languages and modalities with weaker tokenization heuristics, such as Chinese.
questions.expected_facts: The paper reports larger improvement in settings with weaker tokenization heuristics, including Chinese; it does not establish an advantage for every Chinese workload.

questions.question: Which paper provides a provider-specific Groq rate limit for this application?
questions.expected_facts: None of the three research papers provides a Groq account limit.

questions.question: How does the original Transformer compare recurrence and self-attention in sequential computation?
questions.gold_supporting_passage: Self-attention ... connects all positions with a constant number of sequentially executed operations.
questions.expected_facts: Self-attention has constant sequential operations for connecting positions, while recurrent layers require sequential computation across positions.

questions.question: Does Moshi prove that its architecture eliminates all interruptions in real conversations?
questions.gold_supporting_passage: This altogether removes the concept of turn-taking and allows Moshi to handle dynamics including overlap and interruptions.
questions.expected_facts: The paper describes handling overlap and interruptions in its full-duplex design; it does not prove that all interruptions are eliminated.

questions.question: Can these papers determine the correct retry count and exponential-backoff parameters for a Groq client?
questions.expected_facts: The library does not specify provider retry policy parameters.
